description: An alt text policy defines the per-context accessibility rules for all image usage: what contexts require alt text, how decorative images are marked, length limits, prohibited phrases, and AI auto-generation rules.

rules.description: An alt-text-policy.spec.json must exist with a non-empty contexts array where each context has a name.
Every image context must explicitly declare altTextRequired as true or false. Undeclared policy means enforcement is inconsistent across content authors.
Contexts with altTextRequired:false must also declare emptyAltPermitted:true and ariaHidden:true. Decorative images without ariaHidden leak meaningless filenames to screen readers.
Every non-decorative context must define maxLength. Without a length limit, alt text degrades into verbose descriptions that reduce a11y quality.
prohibitedPhrases must be declared and must include: 'image of', 'photo of', 'picture of'. These are the most common useless patterns inserted by content authors.
Every context must declare a cmsField reference. Without it, there is no way to know which CMS field stores the alt text for enforcement.
autoGeneration must be 'allowed' or 'not-allowed'. An absent or undefined value means the policy is unknown, which prevents consistent enforcement.
